behavioral_notes.observation: Each test is a stored record carrying name (Char, translatable), desc (Text), and code_exec (Text, required) — a free-form Python snippet that may run raw SQL via cr.execute or pure Python. The model has no relations and 0 methods of its own: it is a pure data container for an assertion. The default code_exec template merely lists account_journal codes. The model is the configurable 'rule' half; the report model does the running. _order='sequence'.

The AbstractModel report executes each test's code_exec with safe_eval(mode='exec') inside a sandboxed context exposing cr (db cursor), uid, a reconciled_inv() helper, and an empty 'result' slot. The snippet is expected to assign 'result'; an empty/falsy result is rendered as 'The test was passed successfully' (PASS), while a non-empty list/tuple/set is formatted row-by-row as the FAILURE detail. An optional 'column_order' variable controls field display order when result rows are dicts. This is how pass/fail is derived — there is no boolean flag, the emptiness of result IS the verdict.

The QWeb report (report_account_test_templates.xml) iterates docs (the selected accounting.assert.test records) and, per test, prints name + desc then t-foreach over execute_code(o.code_exec), rendering each returned line. So the report runs the assertion live against the current ledger at render time and prints the outcome inline; nothing is persisted. Report timestamp is datetime.now().

accounting.assert.test has active (Boolean, default True) and sequence (Integer, default 10) with _order='sequence', so tests run/display in sequence order and archived (active=False) tests are excluded by the default ORM domain — letting an auditor curate which integrity checks run and in what order without deleting them.

Ships ~6 active standard assertions as data records: Test 1 'General balance' (SUM(debit)-SUM(credit)=0 over account_move_line), Test 3 'Movement lines' (per-move balance + am.date=ml.date), Test 5.1/5.2 (reconciled invoices vs Payable/Receivable accounts), Test 6 'Invoices status' (paid/reconciled invoices not left in Open state), Test 7 'Closing balance on bank statements' (balance_start + sum(lines) = balance_end_real). Two more (Test 4 reconciliation, Test 8 account.period) are commented out as TODO since their underlying models changed. Several queries reference legacy tables (account_invoice, account_bank_statement) not present in the current account schema.

0 JS files, 0 OWL components, 0 registry registrations, 0 patches, no asset bundles. UI is entirely server-rendered: a list/form/search on accounting.assert.test plus a QWeb PDF report; menu under Accounting reporting, gated to base.group_no_one (developer/debug mode only).
0 outbound HTTP call sites; no SDK imports; uses_api_keys=False; no endpoints. Fully self-contained — reads the local Odoo database only.

classification.rationale: account_test is a financial-controls / audit utility extending account with no business object of its own: accounting.assert.test is a pure rule container and report.account_test.report_accounttest is a read-only renderer that runs each rule's code_exec against the ledger. It creates no primary value and owns no document in any value chain — it is a support activity that safeguards the integrity of the system of record. APQC 9.0 Manage Financial Resources, specifically the internal-financial-controls / general-accounting-quality strand (9.x 'Manage internal controls' / record-to-report assurance): it audits the double-entry books produced by account (balanced entries, reconciliation, posted vs draft, bank-statement closing balances). It could be argued under 11.0 (Manage Enterprise Risk, Compliance & Resiliency) as an internal-control test harness, but its scope is strictly the financial ledger and it depends only on account, so 9.0 is the closer fit; 11.0 is the secondary reading.
